guide.title: Bleeding Control
guide.lead: Bleeding is the most preventable cause of trauma death. Press hard, use a tourniquet early for life-threatening limb bleeding, and pack junctional wounds. Then think about where you can't see the blood: chest, belly, pelvis and long bones.

steps.title: Limb: tourniquet
steps.text: 5–7 cm (2–3 inches) above the wound, not over a joint. Tighten until the bleeding stops and the distal pulse disappears. Write the time.

steps.title: Still bleeding?
steps.text: Tighten more; add a second tourniquet above the first. Never loosen it in the field.

steps.title: Junctional (groin, armpit, neck)
steps.text: Pack the wound with hemostatic or plain gauze; press at least 3 minutes; pressure dressing.

steps.title: Tranexamic acid
steps.text: Within 3 hours of injury, per protocol.

sections.title: Where else is the blood?
rows: Rapid transport; massive hemothorax is 1500 mL or more
Distension, tenderness, seat-belt sign, Kehr's sign
Pelvic pain, Grey Turner's bruising, shock

sections.title: No longer recommended
items: Improvised tourniquets when a commercial one is available

quiz.q: Spurting forearm bleeding continues despite firm pressure. Next?
quiz.explanation: Not over a joint; write the time.

quiz.q: Left shoulder pain after a blow to the left upper abdomen. Suggests:
quiz.explanation: Blood under the diaphragm irritates the phrenic nerve.

options: Tighten until bleeding stops and the distal pulse disappears; never loosen in the field

quiz.q: Deformed femur, tender pelvis, BP 88/60, HR 130, distended abdomen. Blood loss?
options: Several litres: femur, pelvis and abdomen together
quiz.explanation: Femur 1–1.5 L; pelvis can exceed 2–3 L.

options: Pack the wound and press firmly for at least 3 minutes

quiz.q: Tranexamic acid must be given within:
Tourniquet still leaking after full tightening:
options: Add a second tourniquet above the first

quiz.q: Bright red spurting blood is from:
quiz.explanation: Venous bleeding is dark and steady.

quiz.q: Massive hemothorax is blood in the chest of at least:
quiz.explanation: Dull percussion, reduced breath sounds, shock.

quiz.q: Which bleeding method is no longer recommended?

flashcards.question: Arterial, venous, capillary bleeding
flashcards.answer: Arterial: bright red, spurting. Venous: dark, steady. Capillary: oozing.

flashcards.question: Sequence for external bleeding
flashcards.answer: Direct pressure → tourniquet (limb) or packing (junctional) → pressure dressing. Elevation and pressure points are no longer recommended.

flashcards.question: Applying a tourniquet
flashcards.answer: 5–7 cm above the wound, not over a joint; tighten until bleeding stops; write the time; never loosen in the field; add a second if needed.

flashcards.question: Kehr's sign
flashcards.answer: Left shoulder pain from blood under the diaphragm: think spleen.

flashcards.question: Fracture blood loss
flashcards.answer: Femur 1–1.5 L; tibia or humerus about 0.5–0.75 L; pelvis can exceed 2–3 L.

flashcards.question: Signs of internal bleeding
flashcards.answer: Distension, tenderness, bruising (seat-belt, Cullen's, Grey Turner's), Kehr's sign, unexplained tachycardia, narrowing pulse pressure, cool pale skin, anxiety.

flashcards.question: "On the floor and four more"
flashcards.answer: External bleeding, plus chest, abdomen, pelvis/retroperitoneum and long bones.

flashcards.question: Wound packing
flashcards.answer: Find the bleeding point, pack gauze deep and tight until full, press at least 3 minutes, then a pressure dressing.

critical.scenario: A saw cut to the lower leg spurts despite 5 minutes of pressure; gauze soaked. BP 96/62, HR 124. Trauma centre 35 minutes away.
critical.question: Next step?

options.t: Commercial tourniquet above the wound (above the knee if needed), tighten until bleeding stops, write the time, transport

critical.explanation: Tranexamic acid per protocol if within 3 hours.
critical.kpi: Escalates to tourniquet for uncontrolled extremity hemorrhage

critical.scenario: High-speed crash: seat-belt bruising, deformed left femur, tender pelvis. During transport BP falls from 104/68 to 86/54, HR 132, new confusion. 18 minutes to go.
critical.question: Likely source and priority?

options.t: Pelvic and abdominal bleeding: pelvic binder at the greater trochanters, small fluid boluses to systolic 80–90 mmHg, pre-alert, keep warm
The femur only: traction splint and more fluid
options.f: The pelvis and abdomen are bigger risks.

options.t: Large boluses to a normal BP
Stop and do a full survey

critical.explanation: Pelvic bleeding can't be controlled in the field; the binder reduces the volume.
critical.kpi: Identifies occult pelvic/abdominal hemorrhage and applies pelvic binding

critical.scenario: Mid-upper-arm amputation: a bystander's tourniquet looks loose and the stump bleeds briskly. BP 84/50, HR 138, barely responsive.
critical.question: Next action?

options.t: Tighten it; if bleeding continues, a second tourniquet above it; pressure on other wounds; permissive fluids; rapid transport
Remove it and start again from scratch
Pressure dressing over the stump only
Aggressive fluids to systolic above 100 mmHg

critical.explanation: Bring the amputated part wrapped in moist gauze, bagged, on ice.
